Department of Mathematical Sciences
The Department of Mathematical Sciences All major areas of mathematics are represented at the dept on major areas of mathematics: Algebra, Analysis, Topology, Geometry, and Applied Mathematics. It is in charge of education in basic mathematics for non-math majors as well as more specialized mathematics for math majors. The Research Institute of Mathematics is a center of active research on diverse areas of mathematics.
· Loc : Bldg. 27 Room 119
· TEL : +82-2-880-6530, 6531, 5857
· Fax : 02-887-4694
· Email : math@snu.ac.kr
View detail

Department of Statistics
Statistics is a field that studies the entire process from research on uncertainty to decision-making based on learning from data. Due to the development of information and communication technology, the amount of data is increasing at a rapid pace, and large data in unstructured forms that cannot be applied to existing analytical methods are emerging in fields such as genomics, climatology, neuroscience, medicine, finance and economy. Statistics seeks to extract new information from these unstructured large data and to obtain new scientific discoveries and social value from them.
· Loc : Bldg. 25
· TEL : +82-2-880-6566(6565)

· Email : stat@snu.ac.kr

Department of Physics & Astronomy (Physics)
Our aims are to discover the fundamental principles of nature, to understand various physical phenomena using basic principles, and eventually to contribute to scientific and technical innovation. We have been the leader of not only physics but also science and technology in Korea since its inception in 1946. At present, we have about 40 regular faculty members and 50 research associates along with 280 undergraduates and 400 graduate students.

Dept. of Biological Sciences
"As a first decade of the 21st century passes away, we are witnessing the ever-growing public interest in biomedical research and break-through researches unraveling the mysteries of life.
Since working with living organisms is complicated and the secrets of life are too complex for a single biological discipline to fully decipher, more and more, the biological research requires collaboration, sharing of ideas and knowledge with other disciplines in natural sciences as well as with the fields of humanities and social sciences. Therefore, current biology has become a truly multi-faceted science, all of which sub-disciplines must achieve collateral advancement. One of the goals in the Department of Biological Sciences at Seoul National University is to pursue the understanding of biological phenomena at the molecular, cell, tissue, individual and environmental levels. It also provides key knowledge that can be widely applied to healthcare, industry, and environmental research and business."

Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences
Brain and cognitive science is to study the biological mechanisms of cognition and to develop the neural techniques to improve and modulate behavior and cognition. Brain and cognitive sciences target various levels for scentific investation, from the individual neuronal level to the systems level, to uncover the information processing patterns of the brain. The principles and techniques discovered during the process should help the society and individuals cope with various mental problems and develop brain-like AI in the future.

Interdisciplinary Graduate Program for History and Philosophy of Sciences provides education and research on the nature, foundations, origins, and place of science in contemporary politics, culture and society. In addition to graduate major courses, it provides liberal arts and major courses for undergraduate students.

Interdisciplinary Graduate program in Gebetic Engineering
Interdisciplinary Graduate Program for Genetic Engineering was created in 1984 as an interdisciplinary graduate program for molecular biology for the purpose of education and research on molecular biology, which was the cutting edge area in life sciences. As Research Institute of Molecular Biology and Genetics was established in 1991 and the need to train professional personnel increased, the name of the program was changed to Interdisciplinary Graduate Program for Genetic Engineering in 1994 and the doctoral program was established in 1996. Currently, it is operated mainly by professors from · Research Institute of Molecular Biology and Genetics, Faculty of Life Sciences, College of Medicine, College of Dentistry, College of Pharmacy, College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, and College of Education.
